facts.fact: PhpSpreadsheet publishes the same ten high-J0 decimal coefficients and the same ten high-J1 decimal coefficients as the pinned SheetJS source. Its J0 first nonconstant amplitude coefficient is -0.1098628627e-2; its J1 first two are 0.183105e-2 and -0.3516396496e-4. The phase constants0.785398164 and2.356194491 and scale0.636619772 also agree. This independently published permissive file supplies no changed-coefficient explanation.
FormulaJS delegates the Bessel functions to the bessel dependency, declared as version range^1.0.2. It supplies no separate numerical coefficient table and is not an independent coefficient lineage.

Fullerton's published high-J0/J1 family uses Chebyshev approximations to modulus and phase, with argument regions4 through8 and above8. The stored tables have37 or40 amplitude coefficients and39 or44 phase coefficients. It is structurally different from the five-coefficient SheetJS amplitude and phase-correction polynomials. No alternate short-polynomial literal was recovered from these files.

The inspected Cody and Boost sources identify Hart et al., Computer Approximations(1968), as their large-argument origin. Their high-J0/J1 amplitude corrections are rational coefficient families, rather than the short SheetJS polynomial tables. These are independently published permitted alternatives, but this source-only work did not evaluate their Excel fit.

The inspected Sun source uses rational high-argument correction tables in several argument intervals, with trigonometric phase identities. It supplies no changed short-polynomial literal explaining the reported discrepancy.

Hankel's expansion gives leading amplitude corrections -9/(128*x^2) for J0 and15/(128*x^2) for J1. In powers of(8/x)^2 these leading coefficients are -9/8192 and15/8192. These exact asymptotic coefficients are not substitutes for a published finite-interval approximation table.
